g.text: The boundary is drawn at the latency budget, not at ideology
Everything off the critical path is a normal distributed system. Everything on it shares one address space.
ON the critical path - one process, one server, shared memory
mmap'd shared-memory event bus /dev/shm - 0.1 to 1 us
an RPC would be the hop
OFF the critical path - normal services
What 'microservices' actually bundles - and which halves cost latency
The components ARE cleanly separated - just not by a network. Recognising that only the last two properties cost latency is
what makes this a considered choice rather than a rejection of modern practice.
Trading flow - and what is deliberately ABSENT from it
no database write persistence happens by replaying the sequenced event stream, off the hot path
no logging even a formatted log line costs microseconds and can block on I/O - the event stream IS the log
no RPC to risk or wallet both read local memory; their rules and balances are pushed in ahead of time
no lock one thread owns the path, so the concurrency control is the ABSENCE of concurrency
That split - a synchronous check against a local replica, with the authority staying remote and pushing updates - is the general
technique for getting a dependency off a latency-critical path.
